detailed_description: Freelance Rate Calculator turns target take-home income, annual expenses, tax reserve, billable hours per week, weeks off, and currency into estimated hourly rate, day rate, monthly revenue, and yearly revenue. Use it to pressure-test pricing assumptions before you turn them into proposals or retainers.
usage_steps: Enter the annual take-home income you want after expenses and tax reserve.
Add annual business expenses, tax percentage, billable hours per week, weeks off, and currency.
Review the estimated hourly rate, day rate, monthly revenue target, yearly revenue target, and annual billable hours.
Adjust billable hours or weeks off to see how capacity changes the rate you need to charge.
usage_examples: Estimate a consulting hourly rate when you know your annual income goal and planned time off.
Compare a 20-hour and 30-hour billable week before setting a day rate.
Build a quick pricing note for a proposal, then refine it with your real costs and market positioning.

faqs.question: Is Freelance Rate Calculator free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Freelance Rate Calculator runs free in your browser and does not require an account.

faqs.question: Does this replace tax or accounting advice?
faqs.answer: No. It is a planning calculator for rate assumptions. Ask a qualified professional about taxes, legal structure, and accounting rules.

faqs.question: What counts as billable hours?
faqs.answer: Billable hours are hours you expect clients to pay for, not every hour you work. Admin, sales, learning, and unpaid support usually reduce billable capacity.

faqs.question: Why does the rate rise when I take more weeks off?
faqs.answer: The calculator spreads the same annual revenue need across fewer billable weeks, so the hourly and day rate increase.
